proof_summary: For primes \(p,q\) with different final digits, \(pq\le150\), and neither dividing \(d\), invertibility of \(d\bmod pq\) yields an \(i<pq\) for which \(pq\mid a+id\), making that term inadmissible. A finite divisibility case analysis using \(2,3,5,7,11,13,17\) shows that covering all such prime pairs would force \(d\) to contain a product of distinct prime factors exceeding \(2025\), a contradiction.
